name: _debug_has_internal_overlap
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_debug_has_internal_overlap(Tensor self) -> int. This is the only supplied registered overload, but it is representative and not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and no test may be removed or narrowed to fit this single signature. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: ["aten::_debug_has_internal_overlap(Tensor self) -> int"]. Semantics: classifies the internal-overlap status of a tensor's layout and returns a plain Python int code, where 0 means no internal overlap, 1 means an axis of size > 1 carries stride 0 (a broadcast), and 2 means the strides alone cannot decide whether elements alias (indeterminate, not proof of overlap). The classification is defined on layout metadata (sizes, strides, storage_offset) rather than element values, the result is a plain int compared directly and not wrapped in a tensor, no argument is mutated or aliased, and there is no differentiable (backward) or elementwise/reduction semantics. The pytest exercises contiguous, transposed, permuted, narrowed, channels-last, size-1 zero-stride, expand/as_strided broadcast, step-sliced, diagonal and overlapping as_strided layouts, plus scalar, empty and sparse COO tensors, over the supported dtype list and the shared value-range and special-value scenarios, and in every case compares the returned code with the native reference instead of asserting a fixed code for a given layout. Non-tensor arguments (None, float, int, str, list) and wrong arity (0 or 2 tensor arguments) are rejected by pytest with TypeError/ValueError/RuntimeError; those error and arity behaviours remain owned by the original pytest and are not expressed by this definition. Tensor outputs are logical single returns; the int scalar return is modeled as one logical output named 'out'.
